Real Estate Workers’ Walkout Halts Projects Across Bengaluru

Bengaluru, June 20 – Thousands of real estate workers across Bengaluru have staged a walkout for the second consecutive day, bringing ongoing development and sales activities to a grinding halt in one of India’s fastest-growing property markets. The strike, called by the Karnataka Real Estate Workers’ Union (KREWU), has seen participation from site supervisors, sales staff, and back-office workers employed by more than 30 real estate firms, including major players like UrbanNest Developers and Greenfield Realty.

The workers are demanding improved wages, formal contracts, and better workplace safety measures. "We have been negotiating for months, but there has been little progress. Our members are essential to every project, from planning to handing over keys, but their concerns have not been addressed," said KREWU President Shyam Sundar.

As a result, construction has stalled at over 60 residential and commercial projects, and sales offices remain shuttered. Prospective buyers who visited sites reported seeing locked gates and empty marketing suites. "We had scheduled a site visit for our new office space today, but the developer informed us that all appointments are cancelled until further notice," said Rajeev Menon, a local business owner.

Industry analysts warn that the disruption could deal a blow to project deadlines and cash flows. “Most firms operate on tight schedules. Even a short walkout can delay possession dates and impact revenue projections,” said Meera Patil, a property market consultant.

The Bengaluru Real Estate Association has called for urgent talks to resolve the standoff. "We recognize the workers' contributions and are committed to constructive dialogue. However, we urge the union to return to work while discussions continue," said Association Secretary R. K. Narayan.

As the strike enters its third day, both sides remain at an impasse, leaving the city’s skyline dotted with silent cranes and unfinished towers. Union leaders have said the strike will continue until their demands are met.
